text:
jordan: noticing a spike in 5xxs from inference pods in eu-west-1. they all started failing outbound calls to S3 and our rollout-check webhook around 09:00 UTC. not sure if this is a routing/egress thing or new sidecar config

maria: ugh. saw similar in staging yesterday after the istio upgrade. can you paste the pod logs + envoy errors?

jordan: here are the envoy errors from one pod: 
[2026-03-17T08:59:58Z] error envoy config: route rejected: outbound cluster not found for host "s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com"
[2026-03-17T08:59:58Z] connection refused to 169.254.169.254:80 (metadata)

lee: that first one screams outboundTrafficPolicy restrictive. did we flip meshConfig.outboundTrafficPolicy.mode to REGISTRY_ONLY in eu-west?

jordan: looks like it. coord with infra-deploys history: the istio helm chart bump added default to REGISTRY_ONLY to harden egress. Not all services have egress rules yet.

ashley: quick check — can you run this and paste output?
jordan: running:
```
kubectl -n inference exec -it inference-pod-57 -- curl -v https://s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/healthcheck || true
kubectl -n istio-system get configmap istio -o yaml | yq .data.mesh | sed -n '1,120p'
```

jordan: curl hangs, envoy logs show 503 with upstream connect error. mesh config snippet: 
"outboundTrafficPolicy:
  mode: REGISTRY_ONLY"

oliver: confirmed. REGISTRY_ONLY blocks direct DNS to external clusters unless a ServiceEntry exists. We have ~12 services missing ServiceEntry for S3 and metadata endpoints.

maria: options: 1) add ServiceEntry objects for S3 + metadata in eu-west (explicit whitelist). 2) set outboundTrafficPolicy mode to ALLOW_ANY (global) as a fast rollback. 3) route those pods through an egress gateway and allow egress from the gateway.

lee: pros/cons: 1 is safest long-term but tedious and easy to miss new domains. 2 is fastest but relaxes policy cluster-wide. 3 is good security-wise but needs egress gateway infra (and we don't have one in eu-west yet).

ashley: can we do a hybrid: temporarily ALLOW_ANY for eu-west to restore traffic, then follow up with ServiceEntry rollout + egress gateway design?

jordan: yes i can escalate to mitigation. would prefer to avoid global change across other regions.

ops-bot: incident created: INFR-2026-047 - Sidecar egress policy blocking outbound traffic in eu-west-1. severity: high.

maria: action plan: 
• jordan: patch istio meshConfig in eu-west to ALLOW_ANY and monitor (temp rollback)
• ashley: open a repo draft PR adding ServiceEntry manifests for s3, sts, metadata endpoints and a checklist for new external hosts
• lee: design egress-gateway terraform + helm in a small RFC and estimate rollout time

jordan: applying patch now:
```
kubectl -n istio-system patch configmap istio -p '{"data":{"mesh":"outboundTrafficPolicy:\n  mode: ALLOW_ANY\n"}}' --type merge
kubectl -n istio-system delete pod -l app=istiod || true  # force reload
```

jordan: patch applied, istiod restarted, telemetry shows curl succeeding again to s3 (first successful at 09:05 UTC). 5xx rate dropped to baseline.

ashley: thanks. can you capture before/after graphs and post to the incident ticket? also please add a note in release notes about the istio upgrade change and the need for ServiceEntries.

oliver: long term we should: 
- ship an allowlist operator that auto-generates ServiceEntry for well-known cloud endpoints per region
- add e2e test in infra-ci that deploys a pod and verifies outbound access to common cloud endpoints after mesh upgrades

lee: agreed. i'll pick up the e2e test and infra-ci changes.

maria: one gotcha: some apps rely on instance metadata (169.254.169.254). ServiceEntry doesn't cover link-local addresses; for metadata we should either route via egress gateway or use a node-proxy. add to RFC.

jordan: will monitor and leave ALLOW_ANY for 2 hours, then we can either keep it w/ a scheduled task or roll back once ServiceEntries are applied.

ashley: i'll create the PR and tag eng-security + infra for review. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

oliver: filing follow-ups in INFR-2026-047: add checklist items and owner labels. closing thread here but keep the incident ticket open.
